title: The factory's GH_TOKEN lacks 'workflow' scope: any push touching .github/workflows/* is rejected outright
body: `git push` fails with 'refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow ... without workflow scope' the moment a commit in the push touches any file under .github/workflows/, even if other files in the same push are fine — GitHub rejects the whole push, not just that file. `gh auth refresh -s workflow` cannot fix it here because GH_TOKEN is an env var, not a stored gh credential, so gh refuses to refresh it non-interactively.
resolution: Keep workflow-file edits out of any commit you intend to push from this token. Leave the diff unstaged/uncommitted (or in a separate local-only commit) and hand the exact diff to the human in the PR description instead, asking them to apply it directly with a token that has the scope.

title: Golden VMs resolve agent-then-repo, warm tier is a speed-up only
body: agents.resolve_snapshot (control/agents.py) picks, in order: `golden-<agent>--<owner-repo>` (warm tier, repo pre-cloned) if it exists, else `golden-<agent>` (agent image, no repo), else nothing — dispatch fails rather than borrowing a mismatched golden. Every run installs its repo's dependencies itself whichever snapshot it booted from: step 2 of the run prompt in control/runner.py is "Install this project's dependencies, before you touch any code", and the prompt says plainly that "nothing is installed for this repo yet". scripts/refresh-golden.sh states it from the other side: "A warm golden is a speed-up; every run installs for itself". So a missing warm snapshot costs minutes, not correctness.

title: Priming receipts are one FACTORY_MEMORY log line, parsed permissively and never persisted
body: control/runner.py defines MEMORY_RECEIPT_MARKER + parse_memory_receipt: the build prompt requires one `FACTORY_MEMORY {"indexed":n,"opened":[...],"domains":[...]}` line right after memory priming (an explicit EMPTY_MEMORY_RECEIPT when .mem/ is absent), and the parser scans free-form run output for the marker, tolerating anything before or after it. Malformed JSON, wrong field types, or no marker at all -> None, never a raise. This module only builds the prompt and parses the line; it does not write telemetry.memory_reads (that storage seam already exists in telemetry/store.py from #49 and is wired up by a later factory-memory-foundation step) and does not judge which memories were useful.

title: Control plane runs on a Hetzner VM under systemd, not on boxd itself
body: The control plane moved off boxd on 2026-08-19 after the box it ran on had its root filesystem corrupt, taking run history with it: the thing the factory forks VMs *from* should not also be the thing that remembers what it did. Deploy is `scripts/deploy.sh` (pulls tracked branch, rebuilds, restarts `factory.service`); TLS is Caddy, not boxd's proxy; secrets live only in `.env` on the box. boxd is still where every run VM comes from — the Hetzner box only talks to it over the API (BOXD_API_KEY).

title: Memory receipts persist from _stream, scanning decoded JSON event text not raw wire lines
body: control/runner.py now wires the FACTORY_MEMORY receipt (mem_6a59) to telemetry: _stream watches every JSON stream-json event for a receipt and, on the first valid one, calls telemetry.store.write_memory_reads (one row per opened id) inside a try/except that only logs on failure (AC4) — a receipt never fails or stops the run. The receipt line is NOT a raw wire line like the FACTORY-MANIFEST prefix (which the shell script echoes outside the agent); the agent prints it as its own turn text or via a shell echo, so it only exists with real newlines after json.loads(line) decodes the assistant message content blocks (text and tool_result). Scanning the raw undecoded line (as parse_memory_receipt alone would if fed the wire text) misses it because `\n` is still two characters there. See runner._receipt_candidates. telemetry.store.memory_metrics_by_repo() (new) joins memory_reads to runs.repo, the same table unit_economics already reads, to avoid a second source of repo truth; usage_for_run() now also returns a `memory` key.

title: Admission-control tables (e.g. memory_candidates) live in control/db.py as INSERT OR IGNORE plus an explicit transition-edge dict
body: For issue #52 (memory_candidates), the queue followed control/db.py's existing repos-table shape: idempotent insertion via `INSERT OR IGNORE` on the primary key (fields dict includes id, so a resubmission is silently dropped and the first insert's fields win), and status transitions gated by a plain `dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]` of allowed edges (e.g. {"pending": ("accepted", "rejected")}) rather than a state machine library. transition_candidate() raises ValueError on any disallowed edge (including repeating a terminal transition) rather than returning False, so callers can't mistake "no-op" for "just happened". Tests follow control/repos_test.py's shape: point settings.db_path at a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() via object.__setattr__ (settings is frozen), then asyncio.run(db.init()) once at module scope.

title: boxd's snapshots.create only queues the capture; reaping the machine aborts it
body: The SDK's `boxd.snapshots.create(machine_id, name)` returns once boxd has QUEUED the capture, not once it has been written. `control/provision.py` destroyed the machine in its `finally` immediately after, which aborts the capture permanently: the name is left in the fleet at `pending` with no version, `agents.available()` correctly refuses to dispatch onto it (restorable means `bool(version)`, never `status == 'ready'`), and the repos register meanwhile says the repo is warm. The live symptom was `golden-mithril-studio-software-factory v0 pending 0B` with no machine behind it while every run for that repo still booted `golden-copy`. `scripts/build-golden.sh` never hit it because the `boxd snapshots save` CLI blocks until the capture lands. Any code path that captures a snapshot must wait via `agents.wait_until_captured(boxd, name, was, timeout, poll)` before deleting the machine, and must compare against the version the name carried BEFORE the capture — a re-save publishes a new version under a name that already has one, so testing for mere existence returns instantly and reproduces the bug. A capture that never lands is deleted rather than left in the fleet. Stubs in tests must model the delay (`control/warm_golden_test.py` `Snapshots`): a stub that publishes the finished snapshot synchronously cannot express this bug, which is why the ordering assertion `snapshots.create before machines.delete` passed for as long as the bug was live.

title: An empty FACTORY_MEMORY receipt is persisted, and stays provisional until one opens a record
body: The empty receipt exists so 'primed, opened nothing' and 'never reached step 1' do not look the same downstream, so it is written to `memory_receipts` even with no reads to attribute. It is also held provisionally: the build prompt spells the empty receipt out as valid JSON for an agent to copy, so anything echoing the prompt back through the stream carries a parseable receipt, and stopping at the first match let that echo claim the run. `_better_receipt` keeps listening until a receipt opens a record; the run-level row REPLACEs and the per-record rows IGNORE, so an upgrade costs one extra write and no wrong row.

title: Memory candidates: build-only env var, collected before both reaps, id derived from run + content
body: A run proposes learnings by appending JSONL to $FACTORY_MEMORY_CANDIDATES, and control reads the file out of the VM before it is destroyed. Three things are not obvious. The variable is set on build runs only (dispatch_env's `kind`), because the review prompt never asks for the file and an env var naming a file nobody collects invites writing into a void — vm_script_test pins the build/review env difference, so adding one means editing that list. Collection is called twice, after _salvage_transcript and again in the finally before the fallback reap, with a `collected` flag: the ordinary path misses every run that died in the stream, and that run's VM is reaped in the finally. The candidate id is sha256(run_id + content), not agent-chosen, so INSERT OR IGNORE deduplicates a double collection instead of silently dropping a second distinct learning that reused an id.

title: The goal is a committed .factory/goal.md tracked by blob SHA; there is no goal API
body: A repo's goal is one committed file, .factory/goal.md, with images and context beside it in .factory/ — the checkout is the only channel that can carry pictures to a plan VM, so the prompt points at the file (plan.goal_prompt) and never splices its content. The control plane stores only the file's blob SHA (repos.goal_sha); plan.sync_goal_file polls it via the contents API on the dry-queue branch, above the budget gate (spend-free) and throttled to one GET per repo per 300s. Any SHA change re-arms the goal to active — including from met/stalled — and resets stalls; deletion clears it to none; an API error makes no transition (unknown is not deleted). Planning is one feature per pass: an agent:feature parent (structure, never queued) plus agent:queued sub-issues; a later plan run closes verified parents. The old textarea goal, its PATCH endpoint and repos.set_goal are gone — do not reintroduce a second goal source.
